issues.detail: The Vietnamese translation ('làm cho... vấp phạm') suggests 'making someone stumble,' whereas the Greek 'σκανδαλιση' (skandalize) in this context specifically means 'causing to stumble/offending' as an action against the believer. More importantly, the Vietnamese phrasing 'thà... còn hơn' (rather... than) adds a comparative structure of preference/concession that is not present in the Greek 'συμφερει' (sypherei), which denotes 'it is better/more profitable' in a direct sense.
